text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: We should prioritize linking core assets from Kaedim, the AI-powered 3D asset production tool, to push link coverage toward 100%. This decision makes sense because Kaedim assets are likely to be high-value and frequently accessed, making them a key part of reaching our goal. By focusing on these assets, we accept the trade-off of potentially delaying the linking of less critical assets, such as those from Gluestack UI MCP Server, at least in the short term. This targeted approach will help us make significant progress toward the 100% link coverage goal, and meet the daily +5% target.

name: Scriv
text: Kaedim’s assets are high-value, but linking them first risks locking us into a single vendor’s format before we validate our own needs. Instead, we should first audit which assets are *actually* missing links—core UI components, not just 3D models—then prioritize the ones that block the bus task. Settle it by running a quick inventory of the current link gaps and mapping them to the bus task’s critical path.

name: Chisel
text:
Link the Kaedim assets first, but only the ones that block the bus task. Kaedim’s assets are high-value and likely to cover the biggest link gaps quickly, pushing coverage up faster than auditing everything. The trade-off is locking into Kaedim’s format early, but we’ll validate the bus task’s needs first to avoid wasted effort.

name: Sift
text: Linking only the Kaedim assets that block the bus task still risks creating dependencies on a format that may not align with broader project needs. A better alternative is to conduct a comprehensive audit first; this ensures a holistic view of all missing links and informs decisions based on actual requirements rather than assumptions. Settling this argument requires data on existing gaps and feedback from the team about what blocks progress most effectively.
